_comment: Release notes shown by cop after an update (what's new since the user's previous version, including skipped versions). 'approved' MUST be true before a version's features are shown to users and before that version is released. When cutting a release, add an entry for the new version, review the features, then set approved=true.

features: cop help and reference.html now render `type X = Base & { ... }` fields; all six `:as<Language>` narrowings are documented and linked.
`:as<Language>` narrowing now applies to Methods and Statements across all 6 languages; added a flat `codebase.Methods` collection.
`cop init --checks`: generate cop checks from your repo's existing instructions via a coding agent.
`cop verify` now statically type-checks call arguments (e.g. flags anchoring `toError` on a non-position before runtime).
Package auto-restore now repairs incomplete/stale cached packages instead of looping on "restored ok" / "not found".
Running a package now uses `cop run <package>`; a mistyped or unknown command shows a clear error (with a suggestion) instead of trying to restore it as a package.
New `sameAs` / `sm` functions: convention-insensitive identifier comparison (ignores case, underscores, and hyphens).
cop now checks once a day for a newer release and shows a persistent reminder to run `cop update`.
After you update, cop prints a concise "what's new" summary — including any versions you skipped.

New built-in analysis for config formats and scripts: YAML (CI workflows, Kubernetes, docker-compose), Dockerfile, XML (.csproj/pom.xml), OpenAPI, SQL, Bash, and PowerShell — each with a ready-to-run check package.
New cross-language SQL injection check flags database queries built from non-constant strings (Python and JavaScript).
TypeScript: `.tsx`/`.jsx` files are now analyzed and `interface`/`enum` declarations are modeled as types.
Language fixes: a `!somePredicate` predicate body and `:any`/`:all`/`:none`/`:count(item ...)` inline expressions now evaluate correctly.
Language fixes: string interpolation now evaluates expressions like `{1 + 2}`; `match` supports the `_` wildcard and case-insensitive arms; verbatim strings `@'\bx\b'` work for regex.

Documented string and object features now work: `.Lower`/`.Upper`/`.Normalized`/`.Words`, object `.Get`/`.Keys`/`.Values`/`:containsKey` with quoted keys, and list `+` append, `.Distinct`/`.Sum`/`.Min`/`.Max`/`.Average`/`.ElementAt`.
`value:function` now invokes the function on the value (e.g. `5:inc`), curried/free-`item` predicates filter correctly, and `foreach` can chain after `&`.
C# provider: `csharp.parse('path')` returns a Codebase and a single `<TargetFramework>` is captured in `Project.Frameworks`.
`cop verify` no longer reports false duplicates for a package overloading or self-importing its own exports, and `cop init` now sets up Copilot CLI hooks.

Module layering now works across Go, Java, Python, and JavaScript: cop discovers each module and its dependencies (e.g. from `go.mod`) and exposes `Project.Name`/`Project.References`, so the `code-layering` package can flag forbidden cross-module dependencies in every language — not just C#.

`cop init --cop-cmd "<invocation>"`: when cop isn't on your PATH (e.g. you run it through mise), the generated agent files and hooks invoke cop your way instead of assuming `cop` on PATH; cop also hints this when it detects a mise config.

Quieter startup: the once-a-day update reminder and post-update "what's new" summary no longer print before `help`/`--version`/`update` output or before an "unknown command" error — a typo now shows just the error.
`cop update` now skips the download when you're already on the latest release (and says so); use `cop update --force` to reinstall.
